analysis:
Both changed files are CI test scripts: scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (new) and scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (the patch updates lane assertions). Neither ships in the provider runtime, so no provider assets (A-001..A-017) or runtime trust boundaries are affected.

The new test runs the route step in a temp dir against a loopback HTTPS plane. The host environment is scrubbed of CURL_*, SSL_CERT_* and proxy variables. It uses a throwaway self-signed cert and calls openssl, curl and jq. It never contacts the production plane: route() raises an AssertionError when routing is on and the URL is empty.

The tests pin these properties of the workflows they read. Workflow files and the router run block are only read, not changed in the supplied units, so I cannot verify them:
- Routing is off unless the switch is exactly 'on'.
- Only https planes are contacted, with certificate verification kept on.
- Fork PRs never contact the plane.
- Only an exact label array for the profile is accepted, otherwise the fallback is used.
- Plane text cannot inject workflow commands or markdown.
- Routed jobs have read-only permissions with no id-token and no secrets, and carry timeouts.
- Release and credentialed workflows keep literal blacksmith runners.
- No workflow other than darkbloom-route.yml mentions self-hosted labels.

These are defensive checks that tighten CI integrity. The patch to test-provider-ci-workflow.py swaps the literal runs-on assertion for the routed fromJSON expression with a fallback, and adds assertions for needs [changes, route] and timeout-minutes 60. That is consistent with the route test and does not weaken any gate.

Remaining question: the actual workflow files (darkbloom-route.yml, ci.yml and others) and the sandbox plane are not in the supplied units. Whether routed self-hosted runners are isolated from credentials and release paths therefore depends on those files and on the plane's deployment. The tests only pin the properties listed above.

I found no security regression in the supplied units.
